messages:
Alex P.: Quick RFC follow-up: proposing a lightweight connection-escrow handshake between the gateway and edge during rolling drains/failovers. goal: preserve priority ordering and avoid head-of-line stalls while we reprovision upstreams.

Nina R.: high level: how is this different from the existing preemptive drain + soft-fail we do today?

Alex P.: today we either accept and serve, or refuse/new conn. with escrow we accept but mark some requests as "escrowed" and keep a small ordered buffer keyed by resume_token so upstreams can pick up midstream without replaying full prompt.

Chen: sounds like a partial-resume token. worried about memory blowup for large KV cache entries or long-running streams. what's the budget?

Alex P.: proposed defaults: escrow_ttl=30s, per-conn buffer cap=1MB, global escrow_quotas per zone. if exceeded we fall back to immediate failover. rationale: short-lived tail safety, not long-term storage.

Marco: how do retries interact? if client retries while we have escrowed partial response, do we dedupe? idempotency keys?

Alex P.: handshake includes resume_token + idempotency_key. gateway will prioritize resuming on same idempotency_key. fallback: if token expired, normal retry semantics apply.

Jules: do we need to change client-facing API? I don't want product teams to wire new headers. keep transparent at gateway edge.

Alex P.: no API change. this is internal between gateway <-> edge proxy. clients still see same behavior except fewer midstream truncations during maintenance.

Chen: metrics and observability: we should emit escrowed_increments, escrow_drop_due_to_quota, resume_success, resume_latency. make SLOs: resume_success >= 99.9 for dedicated.

Marco: testing: need a chaos test that forcibly rotates upstreams midstream and verifies token resume. add an integration harness on staging that simulates partial responses and resume reattach.

Nina R.: security: resume_token must be scoped and short-lived; encrypted with KMS and bound to conn_id + region + model_hash to avoid replay across models.

Alex P.: yep encrypted tokens, HMAC + TTL. also audit events for resume attempts.

Jules: what about batching and KV cache for autoregressive decoders? if we resume into a different replica with different kv layout, can that mismatch semantics?

Alex P.: runtime will only resume to replicas compatible with model_version and quantization_profile. compatible flag in routing table; otherwise we failover to new generation with full re-run.

Chen: keep in mind prefix-caching: we need to snapshot cache pointers, not entire caches. storing a token that references a cache shard + offset should be enough. avoids copying big caches around.

Marco: rollout plan: opt-in flag per cluster, start with non-critical traffic, measure resume_success, memory overhead, tail-latency. then widen.

Jules: ops-bot: can you queue a canary rollout job for us? include metrics in dashboard.

ops-bot: Canary job queued: canary/escrow-handshake v1 -> staging, watch metrics: escrow_resume_success, escrow_memory_bytes, ingress_tail_latency.

Alex P.: action items: 1) prototype token format (chen+nina), 2) runtime check for replica compatibility (marco), 3) staging chaos test (jules), 4) dashboards + alerts (ops). I'll open an RFC PR with details.

Nina R.: +1. will sketch token HMAC and KMS envelope today.

Chen: I'll mock cache-pointer token and memory accounting.

Marco: will add compatibility checks to routing layer and a small feature flag.

Jules: I'll own the staging harness and dashboard.

Alex P.: sweet. thanks all. leaving notes in the RFC PR with the example handshake format: ```
handshake = {
  conn_id: string,
  resume_token: string (kms envelope),
  priority: int,
  escrow_ttl_ms: int,
  idempotency_key?: string
}
```

Jules: one more ask: add an opt-out header we can use for low-latency critical paths to skip escrow. sometimes we want immediate fail rather than buffer.

Alex P.: noted — add `x-edge-escrow: false` header honor.

ops-bot: RFC draft created: https://internal.redwood/escrow-handshake-rfc --> reviewers: Alex P., Nina R., Chen, Marco, Jules

Chen: will comment on the PR with memory calc.

Nina R.: will add token KMS proto.

Alex P.: cool. closing thread, will push PR and link here when ready. :rocket:
